summary: Early failover priority preempting explicit model pin during opaque healthcheck in cross-region canary
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that during a scheduled cross-region canary for acme-recommend-v2, sessions that were explicitly pinned to the full-precision v2 model were served by a quantized variant (acme-recommend-v2-q8).

Impact:
- Several sessions for Acme Retail received truncated or lower-quality recommendations for ~35 minutes during the canary window.
- Customer observed increased billing anomalies due to repeated retries from their side (estimated +12% token usage) and raised an enterprise support escalation.

Environment:
- Prod primary region: us-east. Canary slice targeted us-west.
- Customer using explicit model pin via tenancy header X-Model-Pin: acme-recommend-v2@2026-03-09.

Steps to reproduce (as performed by Support):
1) Initiated test requests with pinned header in us-east to tenant ID for Acme.
2) Triggered canary weight shift in staging controller to simulate cross-region prewarm.
3) Observed routing decisions and fallback selection in logs.

Logs / Observations:
- Edge logs show requests preserving X-Model-Pin header.
- Orchestrator routing decision log lines contained a prioritization score that favored "fallback_priority" when healthcheck state was "DEGRADED-OPAQUE" for the full-precision variant.
- Serving-runtime accepted the routed connection to acme-recommend-v2-q8 and responded with quantized outputs.
- No explicit unpin event in control plane for affected tenants.

Requested outcome:
- Fix routing to respect explicit model pins even when a heuristic health state is "DEGRADED-OPAQUE" unless an explicit failover is requested by customer.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Aisha Patel: Intake from Acme CS. Customer observed lower-quality outputs starting 2026-03-09T22:40Z. Provided request IDs and sample responses to support. Escalating to SRE due to billing impact.

2026-03-10 10:05 - Marco Chen (Support): Reproduced locally with canary slice; pinned header preserved but routing scored fallback higher when health probe returned 'DEGRADED-OPAQUE'. Attaching selection trace.
2026-03-10 14:30 - SRE (Liu Wei): Investigating orchestrator policy matching. Noted recent policy change: tag-based fallback_priority introduced in PR #6124. Running targeted logs across shards.

2026-03-11 08:45 - Customer (Acme): Provided additional telemetry showing increased client retries. Customer requests temporary guard to prevent any automatic demotion of pinned models during their windows.
2026-03-12 16:22 - Marco Chen: Scoped mitigation: toggled routing config 'pin_strict=true' for Acme tenant in us-east while engineering works on fix. Monitoring for regressions.
investigation_notes: Orchestrator policy now evaluates attribute tags first (introduced 2026-02-28) and uses a numeric 'fallback_priority' that can override explicit model_version equality when probe state = DEGRADED-OPAQUE.
Edge preserves X-Model-Pin header; header is forwarded to control plane and reaches orchestrator intact (confirmed by request trace).

Healthprobe returned 'DEGRADED-OPAQUE' due to a transient prewarm timeout on full-precision shard in us-west; this state is brittle and marked by the new probe type as non-fatal but scored lower by routing heuristics.

Routing selection used the following tie-break sequence: candidate_score = base_score + fallback_priority - region_penalty. Because fallback_priority for q8 variant was set intentionally high during canary to bias cost-savings, it exceeded strictness threshold and won selection.
No change to customer pin metadata observed; pin TTL remained valid throughout incident window.
Related PR identified: routing-engine PR #6124 (adjusted tag precedence). Suspected mis-specified unit test for pinned-session path.
resolution_notes: Mitigation applied 2026-03-12: set tenant-level flag pin_strict=true for Acme in control plane to force equality-first routing for pinned sessions; this restored full-precision routing immediately. Engineering reverted the fallback_priority override in staging and opened a targeted fix: ensure 'explicit_pin' wins over tag-based fallback_priority unless an explicit customer opt-in for automatic demotion is set. Fix PR merged to main (https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing-engine/pull/6180) and will be rolled to prod with a canary lift on 2026-03-14. Follow-ups: add unit tests for pinned-session precedence, update canary runbook to document the DEGRADED-OPAQUE probe semantics, and offer Acme a bill credit covering the incremental token usage.
